leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.notes: 17th president; led Valpo for 20 years overseeing significant institutional growth; became president emeritus in 2008; died August 2020.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic and Student Affairs
leaders.notes: 18th president, served July 2008-Sept 2020; launched numerous degree programs and major campus construction; became president emeritus.

leaders.priorTitle: Board of Directors member; retired partner
leaders.notes: Valpo alumna ('81) and trustee who served as interim president Sept 1, 2020-Feb 28, 2021, bridging the gap between Heckler and Padilla.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President, University Counsel, and Secretary
leaders.notes: 19th president, served Feb 28, 2021-Dec 31, 2025; first Mexican-American and first Roman Catholic president of this Lutheran-affiliated university; announced retirement in January 2025.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of Hendricks Chapel and Professor, Maxwell School
leaders.notes: 20th president, effective January 1, 2026, following a national search; an ordained ELCA minister who led Hendricks Chapel at Syracuse since 2017.

statusNote: For-profit online/distance university, not a traditionally self-governed nonprofit. Majority ownership passed from founders Bernie and Rita Turner to venture capitalist Don Ackerman (1991), to Sylvan Learning Systems/Laureate Education (2001-2021), to current owner Adtalem Global Education (2021-present). The top role has alternated between 'President' and a combined 'CEO' title as corporate structure evolved; entries below reflect whoever held the President title.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President of Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Joined Walden as VP of Academic Affairs in 1995 and was named president circa 1999 (exact year not well documented); confirmed as president in 2001 during the Sylvan Learning Systems investment. Walden's president for the 1996-1998 window, if different from Morrison, could not be confirmed in this research pass -- flagged as a gap for a later backfill. Succeeded by Paula Peinovich circa 2003 (inferred boundary).

leaders.priorTitle: Provost
leaders.notes: Held the combined title of President and Provost; left in 2007 amid a reported academic-freedom/governance dispute; succeeded by Jonathan Kaplan.

leaders.priorTitle: Chief Operating Officer, North and South America
leaders.notes: Named president in September 2007; moved up to the newly created CEO role in February 2012 as Cynthia Baum became president.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President
leaders.notes: 9th president, appointed February 2012 as Kaplan moved up to CEO; departed in 2014/2015 to become chancellor of Argosy University.

leaders.priorTitle: Chief Executive Officer
leaders.notes: Resumed the president title alongside CEO after Baum's departure; overall led Walden continuously from 2007 to 2018 across both stints.

leaders.priorTitle: Chief Learning Officer and Vice President of College Administration
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: West Coast University; later Trinity School of Medicine
leaders.notes: 11th president, named April 2019; stepped down mid-2021 to pursue faith-aligned mission work; later became president of Trinity School of Medicine in 2024.

leaders.priorTitle: Chief Executive Officer
leaders.notes: Walden's CEO who additionally stepped in as interim president in August 2021 after Ulmer's departure, until Michael Betz was named president in 2022.

leaders.priorTitle: Partner
leaders.notes: Named president in May 2022 by parent company Adtalem Global Education; previously led higher-education and growth-transformation consulting at McKinsey, and earlier held marketing/strategy executive roles at Strayer University and Ellucian.

statusNote: Catholic liberal-arts university sponsored by the Roman Catholic Diocese of Youngstown; standalone, no parent system.

leaders.notes: Fourth president of Walsh University; his tenure ends right at the 1996 cutoff for this dataset, so his pre-1996 background was not researched in depth per project scope. There appears to be roughly a one-year gap (1996-1997) before Kenneth Hamilton's appointment that is not documented in available public sources.

leaders.priorTitle: Director, School of Business
leaders.notes: Fifth president; led the largest capital campaign in the school's history to that point and oversaw new student housing, an expanded science building, and new graduate programs including an MBA and a master's in physical therapy.

leaders.priorTitle: Chairman, President and CEO
leaders.notes: Sixth president; came to Walsh after a 17-year corporate career following an earlier career as an educator; served 18 years, among the longest tenures of any Ohio private-university president; announced retirement in December 2018.

leaders.priorTitle: Chief Government Relations Officer
leaders.priorInstitution: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory
leaders.notes: Seventh and current president, installed August 2019; a former senior U.S. Air Force officer; the board extended his contract through 2030 as of October 2024.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: 10th chancellor, served 16 years (July 1995-June 2011); resigned to return to teaching, then in 2012 became president of Wichita State University, where he had begun his academic career; died in 2019.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: University of Arkansas at Little Rock
leaders.notes: 11th chancellor; went on medical leave December 31, 2017 following a brain cancer diagnosis and passed away in June 2018 at age 60.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Served as interim chancellor following Belcher's medical leave (from late 2017); stepped back to the provost role and then faculty in October 2019 before becoming president of the University of Lynchburg in July 2020.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: 12th chancellor and WCU's first permanent woman chancellor; elected by the UNC Board of Governors in April 2019; had also briefly served as interim president of Valdosta State University in 2016.
